headline: OpenAI gaining on Anthropic in business users, new data from Ramp indicates
summary: New data from corporate credit card company Ramp shows OpenAI is closing the gap with Anthropic among U.S. businesses, growing faster in Q3 after losing its lead in May.
details: Corporate credit card company Ramp's new data reveals a significant shift in the enterprise AI market. OpenAI, once the dominant leader, is now gaining ground on Anthropic among U.S. businesses. This provides insight into the competitive landscape ahead of potential IPOs.

OpenAI had lost its lead among Ramp's paying business users in May, with Anthropic holding 41% market share to OpenAI's 39%. By July, Anthropic's share grew to nearly 44%, while OpenAI reached almost 40%.

Ramp's dataset covers over 70,000 American businesses, spending billions via their corporate card products. While diverse, Ramp's customer base does skew towards the tech industry, offering a relevant snapshot of enterprise AI adoption.

According to Ramp economist Ara Kharazian, OpenAI is currently growing faster than Anthropic in Q3 to date within this segment. This volatility suggests that enterprise AI spending may not be as "sticky" as investors might hope, with businesses willing to switch providers.

Factors contributing to OpenAI's resurgence include the strong performance of "GPT-5.6 Sol," which is increasingly favored by developers. Conversely, Anthropic's "Fable 5" disappointed in adoption and real-world application due to its price and data retention requirements.

Despite the market share battle, Ramp's data indicates that both companies are likely growing their business revenue as the overall market expands. The percentage of Ramp customers paying for AI services has steadily climbed, reaching nearly 56% by July.

headline: Apple Music will label AI-generated content with visible tags, rolling out soon
summary: Apple Music is set to introduce visible labels for AI-generated tracks, a move announced in March. This initiative aims to clearly identify content created by artificial intelligence for listeners.
details: Apple Music is set to introduce visible labels for AI-generated content, a policy first announced in March. The company has now provided further specifics regarding these new labeling requirements for tracks on its platform.

This move aims to increase transparency for listeners, allowing them to easily identify music created using artificial intelligence. The labels will help distinguish AI-generated tracks from human-created works within the Apple Music catalog.
